definition_zh: 已经；早已；（表示惊讶）这么快就
definition_en: before now or before a particular time, often sooner than expected
core_image: 事情在别人开口之前就已经办完了
scene: 会议还没开始，他桌上的咖啡却已经凉了。By the time we arrived, the meeting had already ended.
sceneCN: 这里 already 是「已经」（第 1 个义项：在某个时间点之前就已发生）；句意为等我们到达时，会议已经结束了。

pos.zh: 副词：已经；早已；这么快就

derivatives.zh: 同源形容词，义为「准备好的」，already 的后一成分即来自它
由 ready 加 -ness 构成，义为「准备就绪；敏捷」

senses.title: Before now or before a stated time
senses.definition: before the present moment or before a particular time already mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 在当下或已提到的某个时间点之前就已发生
senses.example: I have already finished the report, so we can leave.
senses.exampleCN: 我已经写完报告了，所以我们可以走了。
senses.why: The word began as all ready, 'fully prepared'; readiness turned into a statement about time, meaning the thing is done before the clock says so.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初写作 all ready，意为「完全准备好」；「准备就绪」变成了关于时间的陈述，指事情在钟点之前就已完成。

senses.title: Sooner than expected
senses.definition: used to show surprise that something has happened earlier than expected
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示某事比预期更早发生时的惊讶
senses.example: You are already back? That was a short trip.
senses.exampleCN: 你这么快就回来了？这趟出门也太短了。
senses.why: If all ready meant fully prepared, then already can mark a result that arrived before anyone was ready for it, and surprise follows naturally.
senses.whyCN: 如果 all ready 意为完全准备好，那么 already 就能标记一个在任何人准备好之前就到的结果，惊讶也就随之而来。

intro.en: Already is an old phrase that froze into one word, and its two halves still carry their original sense.
intro.cn: already 是一个凝固成单词的古老短语，它的两半仍带着原来的含义。

items.en: Eall meant 'all, entirely', and it still survives as the modern word all.
items.cn: eall 意为「全部、完全」，至今仍以现代词 all 的形式存在。

items.en: Raede meant 'prepared, ready', from a root connected with arranging or advising.
items.cn: raede 意为「准备好的、就绪的」，其词根与安排、建议有关。

items.en: The phrase al redy meant 'fully prepared', and it was said of people and of things.
items.cn: 短语 al redy 意为「完全准备好」，既用于人，也用于物。

items.en: Already shifted from 'fully ready' to 'before the expected time'.
items.cn: already 从「完全准备好」转为「在预期时间之前」。

items.en: The old readiness became a statement about the clock: the thing is done before now.
items.cn: 古老的「就绪」变成了关于钟点的陈述：事情在现在之前就完成了。

items.en: Already now also carries surprise, as in the question are you back already.
items.cn: 现代 already 还带有惊讶，例如问句「你这么快就回来了」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the two source words; the near-meaning group gathers time adverbs with different viewpoints.
note.cn: 形近组收两个来源词；近义组收视角不同的时间副词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning prepared for what is coming.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「为即将到来之事做好准备的」。

entries.definition: The phrase meaning everyone or everything is prepared.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，意为所有人或所有东西都准备好了。

entries.definition: The noun for the state of being prepared.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指准备好的状态。

entries.definition: By now, used mostly in questions and negatives.
entries.definitionCN: 指到如今，多用于疑问句与否定句。

entries.definition: At or before the present moment.
entries.definitionCN: 指在当下或当下之前。

entries.definition: At an earlier time, without the sense of surprise.
entries.definitionCN: 指在更早的时候，不带惊讶意味。

entries.definition: Up to this point in time.
entries.definitionCN: 指直到此刻为止。

normalIntro.en: These hooks take the word back to all ready and then move it onto the clock.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把词带回 all ready，再把它移到钟点上。

normal.en: Already is all ready: everything was prepared before you asked.
normal.cn: already 就是 all ready：你开口之前，一切都已经备好。

normal.en: All ready plus a clock equals done before now.
normal.cn: all ready 加上一个钟点，就等于在现在之前做完。

normal.en: Say already when the result jumps ahead of the plan.
normal.cn: 当结果跑到计划前面时，就用 already。

normal.en: Yet asks whether it has happened; already says it has.
normal.cn: yet 问事情发生了没有；already 说已经发生了。

normal.en: The surprise in already comes from being ready too early.
normal.cn: already 里的惊讶，来自「准备得太早」。

abstract.en: Picture a table set before the guests have even knocked.
abstract.cn: 想象客人还没敲门，桌子就已经摆好了。

abstract.en: Now picture the host opening the door to find them already there.
abstract.cn: 再想象主人开门，发现他们已经到了。

abstract.en: The gap between plan and clock is the space where already lives.
abstract.cn: 计划与钟点之间的落差，就是 already 所住的空间。

examples.en: She had already left when the phone rang.
examples.cn: 电话响的时候，她已经离开了。

examples.en: The train is already full, so we must wait.
examples.cn: 火车已经满员了，我们只能等下一班。

examples.en: Is it midnight already?
examples.cn: 已经到午夜了吗？

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喔，来得早」——喔，来得早，所以已经做完了

root: 古英语 eall（全部）+ rǣde（准备好的）组成的短语 al redy，意为「完全就绪」，十四世纪起转为表示「在预期时间之前」。

sensesIntro.en: The two senses share one timeline: something is finished before the expected point, and the second sense adds surprise to that earliness.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项共享同一条时间线：某事在预期节点之前完成，第二个义项只是给这份提前加上惊讶。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a task is crossed off the list before anyone has asked about it.
core.cn: 核心意象：还没人过问，任务就已经从清单上划掉了。

branches.en: THE CLOCK: the first sense places the action before the present moment.
branches.cn: 钟点线：第一个义项把动作放在当下之前。

branches.en: THE DEADLINE: the action also sits before a stated time.
branches.cn: 截止线：动作也位于某个已说明的时间之前。

branches.en: THE EARLY ARRIVAL: the second sense adds the speaker's surprise.
branches.cn: 提前线：第二个义项加上说话人的惊讶。

branches.en: THE COMPLETION: what is already done needs no further waiting.
branches.cn: 完成线：已经做完的事不必再等。

branches.en: THE MISMATCH: surprise appears where reality outruns expectation.
branches.cn: 错位线：现实跑在预期前面时，惊讶就出现了。

intro.en: Already is a frozen phrase rather than a suffixed form, so its list mixes its two source words and its common frames.
intro.cn: already 是凝固短语而非后缀派生形式，因此条目混合了两个来源词与常用框架。

latinIntro.en: Both halves are native English, so no Latin entry is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分都是本土英语，因此不列拉丁条目。

items.exampleCN: 队伍表现出很高的准备度。

items.example: This is an already known fact.
We are all ready to start.

definition_zh: 也；还；同样地；此外
definition_en: in addition, or in the same way as something already mentioned
core_image: 一件事说完了，又把另一件同类的事添在同一行
scene: 老师讲完要点，又在黑板上补了一行字。She speaks French and also a little German.
sceneCN: 这里 also 是「也；还」（第 1 个义项：在前面内容之外再添一项）；句意为她会说法语，也会一点德语。

pos.zh: 副词：也；还；同样地；此外

derivatives.zh: 同源副词，义为「如此；这样」，also 的第二成分即来自它
由 also 与 ran 构成的复合名词，义为「落选者；表现平平的参与者」

senses.title: In addition
senses.definition: used to add another item, fact, or action to what has just been said
senses.definitionCN: 用于在刚说过的内容之外再添一项事物、事实或动作
senses.example: The library has novels and also a large map collection.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆有小说，还有一大批地图。
senses.why: The old compound meant 'all so, just so'; adding a second item keeps it in the same frame as the first.
senses.whyCN: 这个古老的复合词意为「全都如此、正是这样」；添上第二项，就是让它与第一项处在同一个框架里。

senses.title: In the same way
senses.definition: used to say that a second person or thing does or is the same as the first
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示第二个人或事物与第一个相同或做同样的事
senses.example: Her brother is a teacher, and she is also a teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 她哥哥是老师，她也是老师。
senses.why: The 'so' inside also points back to the first statement, so the second statement simply repeats its shape.
senses.whyCN: also 里的 so 指向前面那句话，因此第二句话只是重复了它的形状。

intro.en: Also began as a two-word phrase meaning 'all so', and the second half still points back to what was just said.
intro.cn: also 最初是一个意为「全都如此」的两词短语，后半部分至今仍指向刚说过的话。

items.en: Eallswa meant 'quite so, just as', literally 'all so', joining eall 'all' and swa 'so'.
items.cn: eallswa 意为「正是如此、就像这样」，字面是「全都如此」，由 eall「全部」与 swa「如此」组成。

items.en: The compound shortened to also and kept the sense of 'in the same way'.
items.cn: 这个复合词缩短为 also，保留了「以同样的方式」的含义。

items.en: Also widened from 'likewise' to 'in addition', the sense that now dominates.
items.cn: also 从「同样地」扩展到「此外」，后者如今成为主要义项。

items.en: Two jobs of the word coexist: adding a second item and marking a similar one.
items.cn: 这个词的两种职责并存：添加第二项，以及标记相似的一项。

items.en: The frame not only but also fixed the additive sense in a balanced pair.
items.cn: not only but also 这一框架把添加义固定在平衡的一对结构里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers its source and near forms; the near-meaning group gathers other additive adverbs.
note.cn: 形近组收它的来源与近形词；近义组收其他表示添加的副词。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning in that way or to that degree.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，义为「以那种方式」或「到那种程度」。

entries.definition: A conjunction or preposition of comparison that looks close to also.
entries.definitionCN: 表示比较的连词或介词，外形与 also 相近。

entries.definition: A noun for someone who took part but did not win.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，指参加了却未获胜的人。

entries.definition: In addition, usually at the end of a clause.
entries.definitionCN: 指另外、也，通常放在句末。

entries.definition: The phrase meaning in addition.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，意为「也、还」。

entries.definition: In the same way, often opening a sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 指同样地，常放在句首。

entries.definition: A formal adverb marking an extra point.
entries.definitionCN: 正式副词，标记额外的一点。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the word on one line and then add a second item to that line.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把词留在同一行，然后在这一行上再加一项。

normal.en: Also is all plus so: the whole statement stands, and one more item joins it.
normal.cn: also 是 all 加 so：整句话成立，再加一项进来。

normal.en: The so inside also points back, so the second item copies the first.
normal.cn: also 里的 so 指回前面，所以第二项复制了第一项。

normal.en: Too sits at the end; also sits in the middle.
normal.cn: too 站在句末；also 站在句中。

normal.en: Not only but also pairs two additions like two weights on a scale.
normal.cn: not only but also 把两个添加物配成一对，像天平上的两个砝码。

normal.en: If you can replace it with as well, also is doing its additive job.
normal.cn: 如果能用 as well 替换，also 就在执行添加的职责。

abstract.en: Picture one line of writing with a second line ruled directly beneath it.
abstract.cn: 想象一行字，下面紧贴着再画一行。

abstract.en: Now picture the two lines sharing the same rhythm and the same shape.
abstract.cn: 再想象两行共享同样的节奏与形状。

abstract.en: The second line is also: present, equal, and additional.
abstract.cn: 第二行就是 also：在场、相等，而且额外。

examples.en: The museum is free and also open late on Fridays.
examples.cn: 博物馆免费开放，周五还延长开放时间。

examples.en: He writes poetry and also teaches music.
examples.cn: 他写诗，也教音乐。

examples.en: The drug is effective and also inexpensive.
examples.cn: 这种药有效，而且便宜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧搜」——欧，搜一搜，还能再搜出一样东西

root: 古英语 eallswā（全都如此），由 eall（全部）与 swā（如此）构成；中古英语缩为 also，义从「同样地」扩展为「此外、也」。

sensesIntro.en: The two senses both add a second member, one by addition and one by similarity.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都在添加第二个成员，一个靠「额外」，一个靠「相似」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a statement is written on one line, and a second statement is ruled beneath it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句话写在一行，第二句话紧贴着写在下面。

branches.en: THE EXTRA: the first sense puts one more thing into the list.
branches.cn: 额外线：第一个义项把又一样东西放进清单。

branches.en: THE MIRROR: the second sense repeats the shape of the first statement.
branches.cn: 镜像线：第二个义项重复第一句话的形状。

branches.en: THE FRAME: both senses keep the new item inside the same grammatical frame.
branches.cn: 框架线：两个义项都把新项目留在同一个语法框架里。

branches.en: THE LIST: addition is the word at its most practical.
branches.cn: 清单线：添加是这个词最实用的形态。

branches.en: THE ECHO: similarity is the older sense, still heard in formal writing.
branches.cn: 回声线：相似是更古老的义项，在正式文字里仍能听到。

intro.en: Also is a shortened compound, so its list gathers the two source words and the frames it commonly fills.
intro.cn: also 是缩短的复合词，条目收集两个来源词以及它常填的框架。

latinIntro.en: The word is native English, so the Latin entry list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属于本土英语，因此拉丁条目为空。

items.example: She is not only clever but also kind.
The plant is also known as fever grass.
The team finished as an also-ran.
items.exampleCN: 这支队伍最终只是陪跑。

definition_zh: 可供选择的事物；替代方案；另类的；非传统的
definition_en: one of two or more possible choices, or something different from the usual way
core_image: 岔路口两条路并排铺开，只能挑一条走
scene: 高速封路，导航给出了另一条绕行的路线。We had no alternative but to take the mountain road.
sceneCN: 这里 alternative 是「可供选择的事物；替代方案」（第 1 个义项：两个或多个可选方案之一）；句意为我们别无选择，只能走山路。

pos.zh: 名词：可供选择的事物；替代方案
形容词：替代的；另类的；非传统的

derivatives.zh: 同源动词，义为「交替；轮流」，也可作形容词「间隔的」
由 alternate 加 -ly 构成，义为「交替地」
由 alternate 加 -ion 构成，义为「交替；轮流」
由 alternate 加 -or 构成，义为「交流发电机」
由 alternative 加 -ly 构成，义为「或者；作为另一种选择」

senses.title: One of the possible choices
senses.titleCN: 可供选择的事物；替代方案
senses.definition: one of two or more things that you can choose instead of another
senses.definitionCN: 可以代替另一事物加以选择的两项或多项之一
senses.example: We need an alternative to plastic packaging.
senses.exampleCN: 我们需要一种能替代塑料包装的方案。
senses.why: Latin alter meant 'the other of two', and the derived noun points to the other road standing beside the first.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 alter 意为「两者中的另一个」，派生的名词指向与第一条路并排站着的那条路。

senses.title: A different way from the usual
senses.definition: describing a style, method, or system that differs from the mainstream or established one
senses.definitionCN: 形容与主流或既有方式不同的风格、方法或体系
senses.example: The band plays alternative rock rather than pop.
senses.exampleCN: 这支乐队玩的是另类摇滚，而不是流行乐。
senses.why: If there is always another road, a whole culture can choose the side road on purpose and call itself alternative.
senses.whyCN: 如果总有一条别的路，一整套文化就能有意选择那条侧路，并称自己为 alternative。

senses.title: A substitute in a system
senses.definition: a replacement item or arrangement that can serve the same function when the first is unavailable
senses.definitionCN: 当首选不可用时能承担同一功能的替换物品或安排
senses.example: The hospital keeps alternative supplies for the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 医院为冬天储备了替代物资。
senses.why: The other of two can also be a spare part: same job, different object, held ready in case the first fails.
senses.whyCN: 两者中的另一个也可以是备用件：同样的功能，不同的物件，备着以防首选失效。

intro.en: Alternative descends from a Latin word for 'the other of two', and the whole family keeps that fork in the road.
intro.cn: alternative 源自拉丁语中表示「两者中的另一个」的词，整个词族都保留着那个岔路口。

items.en: Alter meant 'the other of two', the root of every word in this family.
items.cn: alter 意为「两者中的另一个」，是这个词族每个词的根。

items.en: Alternare meant 'to do one thing and then the other, to take turns'.
items.cn: alternare 意为「做一件事再做另一件、轮流」。

items.en: Late Latin alternativus named a choice that offers one course or the other.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 alternativus 指在两条路径中给出其一的选项。

items.en: French passed the adjective and the noun into English.
items.cn: 法语把这个形容词与名词一起传入英语。

items.en: English alternative first named a choice between two possibilities, then any other option.
items.cn: 英语 alternative 最初指两种可能之间的选择，后来指任何其他选项。

items.en: The word now covers options in travel, energy, medicine and the arts.
items.cn: 这个词如今覆盖旅行、能源、医学与艺术中的各种选项。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin family; the near-meaning group gathers words for choices and substitutes.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁词族；近义组收表示选择与替代的词。

entries.definition: To take turns, or every other one in a series.
entries.definitionCN: 指轮流，或序列中每隔一个的。

entries.definition: In turns, one after the other.
entries.definitionCN: 指轮流地、一个接一个地。

entries.definition: The act of alternating between two things.
entries.definitionCN: 指在两事物之间交替的行为。

entries.definition: One thing that may be chosen among several.
entries.definitionCN: 指可供从若干项中选择的一项。

entries.definition: The act of selecting, or the range of things to select from.
entries.definitionCN: 指选择的行为，或可供选择的范围。

entries.definition: A person or thing that takes the place of another.
entries.definitionCN: 指代替另一人或另一物的东西。

entries.definition: A reserve option used if the first plan fails.
entries.definitionCN: 指首选计划失败时使用的备用方案。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start at a fork in the road and then widen the second road into a style and a spare part.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从岔路口开始，再把第二条路扩展成一种风格与一个备件。

normal.en: Alternative comes from alter, the other of two: one road, then the other.
normal.cn: alternative 来自 alter，即两者中的另一个：一条路，然后另一条。

normal.en: An alternative to plastic is simply the road beside plastic.
normal.cn: 塑料的 alternative，就是塑料旁边那条路。

normal.en: No alternative means the fork has collapsed into a single track.
normal.cn: no alternative 意为岔路塌成了一条道。

normal.en: Alternative rock deliberately chooses the side road.
normal.cn: 另类摇滚故意选择那条侧路。

normal.en: A spare part is an alternative held in reserve.
normal.cn: 备用件就是被留作储备的 alternative。

abstract.en: Picture two roads dividing at a sign, both leading to the same town.
abstract.cn: 想象两条路在指示牌处分开，却通向同一座城。

abstract.en: Now picture one road paved and busy, the other narrow and quiet.
abstract.cn: 再想象一条路铺得平整而拥挤，另一条窄而安静。

abstract.en: Choosing the quiet road is the whole meaning of alternative.
abstract.cn: 选择那条安静的路，就是 alternative 的全部含义。

examples.en: Cycling is a healthy alternative to driving to work.
examples.cn: 骑车上班是开车之外一种健康的选择。

examples.en: The council is looking for alternative sources of energy.
examples.cn: 议会正在寻找替代能源。

examples.en: If the train is canceled, we have an alternative plan.
examples.cn: 如果火车取消，我们还有备选计划。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，特内提夫」——哦，特地另提一份，作为替代方案

root: 拉丁语 alter（两者中的另一个）+ -nare（动词词干）+ -ivus（形容词后缀），经法语 alternatif 进入英语，核心始终是「另一条路、另一个选项」。

sensesIntro.en: The senses keep the same fork: another choice, a different style, and a spare that can take the first one's place.
sensesIntro.cn: 各个义项守着同一个岔口：另一个选择、另一种风格，以及能顶替首选的备件。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two roads split at a sign, and only one can be walked at a time.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条路在指示牌处分开，一次只能走一条。

branches.en: THE FORK: the first sense is simply the other choice standing beside the first.
branches.cn: 岔口线：第一个义项就是与首选并排站着的另一个选择。

branches.en: THE SIDE ROAD: the second sense turns the other road into a whole style.
branches.cn: 侧路线：第二个义项把另一条路变成一整套风格。

branches.en: THE SPARE: the third sense keeps the other object ready for the same job.
branches.cn: 备件线：第三个义项让另一个物件随时承担同一功能。

branches.en: THE SWAP: choice and replacement both depend on two things being interchangeable.
branches.cn: 替换线：选择与替代都依赖两件东西可以互换。

branches.en: THE OUTSIDER: what is alternative may be chosen for difference or kept for emergency.
branches.cn: 局外线：被称为 alternative 的东西，可能因不同而被选，也可能因应急而被留。

intro.en: Alternative is built from the Latin root alter plus suffixes, and its family is rich and productive.
intro.cn: alternative 由拉丁词根 alter 加后缀构成，词族丰富而能产。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base alter and the suffixes -nare and -ivus are visible in the entries below.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 alter 与后缀 -nare、-ivus 在下面的条目中都看得见。

items.exampleCN: 我们找到了更便宜的替代方案。

items.example: Alter ego means a second self.
items.exampleCN: alter ego 意为第二个自我。

items.example: The alternation of seasons is regular.
items.exampleCN: 季节的交替是有规律的。
修理工更换了交流发电机。

items.example: Wind is a form of alternative energy.

definition_zh: 虽然；尽管；但是
definition_en: despite the fact that, or used to introduce a statement that contrasts with what came before
core_image: 先承认一块石头挡路，再抬脚跨过去
scene: 雨下得很大，球场上的比赛却没有停。Although it was raining hard, the match continued.
sceneCN: 这里 although 是「虽然；尽管」（第 1 个义项：承认某个事实后仍推进主句）；句意为尽管雨下得很大，比赛仍继续进行。

pos.zh: 连词：虽然；尽管；但是

derivatives.zh: 同源缩略形式，义为「虽然」，更口语，也可置于句末表示转折
although 的简化拼写变体，多见于非正式书面语

senses.title: Despite the fact that
senses.definition: used to introduce a fact that makes the main statement surprising or less expected
senses.definitionCN: 用于引出一个使主句变得出乎意料或不太顺理成章的事实
senses.example: Although the road was icy, we reached the village before dark.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管道路结冰，我们还是在天黑前到了村子。
senses.why: Old English eall theah joined 'all, even' with 'though', so the word grants a fact fully and then lets the main clause stand anyway.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 eall theah 把「全部、甚至」与「虽然」结合，因此这个词先完整承认一个事实，再让主句照样成立。

senses.title: But on the other hand
senses.definition: used to add a contrasting remark, especially after a positive or confident statement
senses.definitionCN: 用于补充一句形成对照的话，尤在肯定或自信的陈述之后
senses.example: The plan sounds simple, although it will cost a great deal.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划听起来简单，不过它要花很多钱。
senses.why: The concessive grant can also soften a turn: the first clause is allowed, and the second quietly takes the opposite side.
senses.whyCN: 这种让步式的承认也能软化转折：先容许第一句成立，第二句再悄悄站到相反的一边。

intro.en: Although began as a two-word phrase in Old English, and its short partner though has outlived it in speech.
intro.cn: although 在古英语中原本是两词短语，它短小的伙伴 though 在口语里活得比它更久。

items.en: The phrase eall theah meant 'even though', with eall 'all, even' and theah 'though'.
items.cn: 短语 eall theah 意为「即使如此、虽然」，由 eall「全部、甚至」与 theah「虽然」构成。

items.en: The two words fused into al thagh and later although, while the short though survived on its own.
items.cn: 两个词融合为 al thagh，后来变成 although，而短形式 though 独立存活下来。

items.en: Although settled as a single conjunction in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: although 在十四世纪固定为单一的连词。

items.en: Its core job is to admit a fact and then set a contrasting clause against it.
items.cn: 它的核心职责是先承认一个事实，再把一个形成对照的分句放在它对面。

items.en: Although remains more formal than though, especially at the head of a sentence.
items.cn: although 比 though 更正式，放在句首时尤其如此。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the shorter forms; the near-meaning group gathers concessive and contrastive connectors.
note.cn: 形近组收较短的形式；近义组收让步与转折的连接词。

entries.definition: The shorter conjunction, common in speech and at the end of a clause.
entries.definitionCN: 较短的连词，常用于口语，也可放在句末。

entries.definition: A simplified spelling of although used in informal writing.
entries.definitionCN: although 的简化拼写，用于非正式书面语。

entries.definition: A separated spelling that echoes the old two-word phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 分开书写的拼法，回响着古老的两词短语。

entries.definition: A stronger concessive phrase stressing the obstacle.
entries.definitionCN: 更强的让步短语，强调障碍之大。

entries.definition: Conceding a possible or hypothetical case.
entries.definitionCN: 让出一个可能或假设的情形。

entries.definition: Used to contrast two facts, weaker than although.
entries.definitionCN: 用于对照两个事实，语气比 although 弱。

entries.definition: A formal connector contrasting two parallel facts.
entries.definitionCN: 正式连接词，对照两个平行的事实。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep the word's two moves: grant the obstacle, then continue anyway.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子保留这个词的两个动作：先承认障碍，再照样继续。

normal.en: Although is all though: the whole objection is admitted, and the sentence still walks on.
normal.cn: although 是 all 加 though：整个反对意见都被承认，句子却照样往前走。

normal.en: Think of a rock on the path: although names the rock, then steps over it.
normal.cn: 想象路上有一块石头：although 先点出石头，再跨过去。

normal.en: Though is the short twin you use in speech.
normal.cn: though 是口语里用的短双胞胎。

normal.en: Even though makes the rock bigger; although just reports it.
normal.cn: even though 把石头放大；although 只是报告它。

normal.en: If the second clause turns against the first, although is likely at the join.
normal.cn: 如果第二个分句与第一个相反，接缝处很可能就是 although。

abstract.en: Picture a hiker who names the fallen tree and then climbs over it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个徒步者先说出倒下的树，再爬过去。

abstract.en: Now picture the same hiker nodding at the warning sign and continuing.
abstract.cn: 再想象同一个徒步者朝警告牌点点头，继续走。

abstract.en: That nod is although: full acknowledgement, no change of route.
abstract.cn: 那个点头就是 although：完全承认，却不改路线。

examples.en: Although she was tired, she finished the last chapter.
examples.cn: 尽管她很累，还是读完了最后一章。

examples.en: The car is old, although it still runs well.
examples.cn: 这辆车旧了，不过还能跑得很好。

examples.en: Although the instructions were clear, several students made the same mistake.
examples.cn: 尽管说明很清楚，仍有几名学生犯了同样的错误。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，楼兜」——哦，楼兜住了雨，虽然下雨也能继续走

root: 古英语短语 eall þēah（全部如此、即使）融合而成，eall 表「全部、甚至」，þēah 表「虽然」；十四世纪固定为单词 although。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses admit one fact first; the first then continues despite it, the second turns the continuation into a softer contrast.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都先承认一个事实；第一个义项随后照样继续，第二个义项把这种继续变成更柔和的转折。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a walker names the stone blocking the path, then steps over it without changing direction.
core.cn: 核心意象：行人先点出挡路的石头，再不改方向地跨过去。

branches.en: THE GRANT: the first sense fully accepts the opposing fact.
branches.cn: 承认线：第一个义项完全接受相反的事实。

branches.en: THE STEP: the main clause goes forward despite what was granted.
branches.cn: 跨越线：主句尽管有那个让步，仍然向前走。

branches.en: THE TURN: the second sense uses the grant to soften a contrast.
branches.cn: 转折线：第二个义项用让步来软化对照。

branches.en: THE BALANCE: two clauses are weighed, and neither cancels the other.
branches.cn: 平衡线：两个分句被权衡，谁也不取消谁。

branches.en: THE NOD: every branch begins with acknowledgement before argument.
branches.cn: 点头线：每条分支都先承认，再争论。

intro.en: Although is a fused phrase, so its list gathers its parts, its short twin and the concessive frames it shares.
intro.cn: although 是融合的短语，条目收集它的成分、短双胞胎以及共享的让步框架。

latinIntro.en: The word is native English, so the Latin entry list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属于本土英语，因此拉丁条目为空。

items.example: Although it rained, we went out.
items.exampleCN: 虽然下雨，我们还是出门了。

items.example: Even though he was ill, he came.
Even if it snows, we will go.
He likes tea, whereas she prefers coffee.
items.exampleCN: 他喜欢茶，而她更喜欢咖啡。

items.example: While I agree, I have doubts.
items.exampleCN: 我虽然同意，但也有疑虑。

items.example: Altho late, she sent the file.
items.exampleCN: 虽然晚了，她还是把文件发了。

definition_zh: 海拔；高度；高处；（几何）高
definition_en: the height of a place or object above sea level or above a base
core_image: 从海平面向上拉出一条竖线，量到脚下的高地
scene: 飞机爬升到巡航高度，窗外的云已经在脚下。At this altitude, the air is too thin for helicopters.
sceneCN: 这里 altitude 是「海拔；高度」（第 1 个义项：某地高出海平面的垂直距离）；句意为在这个高度，空气对直升机来说太稀薄了。

pos.zh: 名词：海拔；高度；高处；（几何）高

derivatives.zh: 由 altitude 加 -inal 构成，义为「高度的；海拔的」
同源词，由拉丁 altus（高）与 -meter（测量）构成，义为「高度表」
复合名词，义为「高原反应；高山症」

senses.title: Height above sea level
senses.definition: the vertical distance of a place or aircraft above sea level or ground
senses.definitionCN: 某地或飞行器高出海平面或地面的垂直距离
senses.example: The village lies at an altitude of three thousand metres.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子位于海拔三千米处。
senses.why: Latin altitudo turned altus 'high' into a measurable noun, and the measure needs a starting line, which is sea level.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 altitudo 把 altus「高」变成可测量的名词，而测量需要一条起算线，这条线就是海平面。

senses.title: A high place or region
senses.definition: a high area of land, often used in the plural for mountain regions
senses.definitionCN: 地势很高的地区，常用复数指山区
senses.example: Few trees grow at these altitudes.
senses.exampleCN: 在这些高海拔地区，很少有树生长。
senses.why: Once height becomes a place, the plural altitudes simply names the high ground itself.
senses.whyCN: 一旦高度变成一个地方，复数 altitudes 就直接指那些高地。

senses.title: The height of a geometric figure
senses.definition: the perpendicular distance from the base to the opposite vertex or side of a figure
senses.definitionCN: 从图形底边到对角顶点或对边的垂直距离
senses.example: The area of a triangle equals half the base times the altitude.
senses.exampleCN: 三角形的面积等于底乘以高的一半。
senses.why: Geometry keeps the oldest image: a vertical line dropped from the top, measured against the base.
senses.whyCN: 几何学保留了最古老的意象：从顶端垂下一条竖线，以底边为基准来量。

intro.en: Altitude comes from a Latin adjective for 'high', and it still asks for a starting line to measure from.
intro.cn: altitude 来自拉丁语中表示「高的」形容词，至今仍需要一条起算线来测量。

items.en: Altus meant 'high' or 'deep', and it also gave English altimeter and the musical term alto.
items.cn: altus 意为「高的」或「深的」，还给了英语 altimeter 与音乐术语 alto。

items.en: The noun altitudo turned the quality of height into an abstract measure.
items.cn: 名词 altitudo 把「高」这一性质变成抽象的度量。

items.en: French carried the noun into English with the sense of height above a base.
items.cn: 法语把这个名词带入英语，含义是高出某一基准的高度。

items.en: Early English used altitude for height in general, including the height of the sun.
items.cn: 早期英语用 altitude 泛指高度，包括太阳的高度。

items.en: Astronomy and sailing sharpened it into the angle or height above the horizon.
items.cn: 天文学与航海把它精确化为高于地平线的角度或高度。

items.en: Today altitude usually means height above sea level or above the ground.
items.cn: 今天 altitude 通常指高出海平面或高出地面的高度。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the Latin family; the near-meaning group gathers words for height with different frames.
note.cn: 形近组收拉丁词族；近义组收框架不同的「高度」类词。

entries.definition: An instrument that measures height above a surface.
entries.definitionCN: 测量高出某一表面高度的仪器。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning relating to height or altitude.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「与高度或海拔有关的」。

entries.definition: A musical term for a high voice or part, from the same Latin word.
entries.definitionCN: 音乐术语，指高音声部，来自同一个拉丁词。

entries.definition: Height above sea level, often shown on maps.
entries.definitionCN: 指海拔，常标在地图上。

entries.definition: The general word for vertical distance.
entries.definitionCN: 表示垂直距离的通用词。

entries.definition: Great height, often literary or figurative.
entries.definitionCN: 指极高，多用于文学或比喻。

entries.definition: The measured gap straight up or down.
entries.definitionCN: 指垂直方向量出的距离。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep a vertical line and a base, then move that line from a mountain to a triangle.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子保留一条竖线与一个底，再把这条线从高山移到三角形。

normal.en: Altitude contains alt, high: a tall line measured from the base.
normal.cn: altitude 里有 alt，意为高：从底部量起的一条高线。

normal.en: The base can be sea level or the bottom of a triangle.
normal.cn: 这个底可以是海平面，也可以是三角形的底边。

normal.en: High altitude means the line is long and the air is thin.
normal.cn: high altitude 意为这条线很长，空气很稀薄。

normal.en: An altimeter is the instrument that reads that line.
normal.cn: altimeter 就是读这条线的仪器。

normal.en: Plural altitudes turns the measurement into mountain country.
normal.cn: 复数 altitudes 把这个度量变成山区。

abstract.en: Picture a rope dropped from a cliff to the sea and marked in metres.
abstract.cn: 想象一条绳子从悬崖垂到海面，上面标着米数。

abstract.en: Now move the cliff into a triangle and the rope becomes the altitude.
abstract.cn: 再把悬崖移进三角形，绳子就成了高。

abstract.en: The number on the rope is what the word always asks for.
abstract.cn: 绳上的数字，就是这个词始终在追问的东西。

examples.en: The plane climbed to a cruising altitude of ten thousand metres.
examples.cn: 飞机爬升到一万米的巡航高度。

examples.en: At high altitude, breathing becomes difficult.
examples.cn: 在高海拔处，呼吸会变得困难。

examples.en: The triangle has a base of six centimetres and an altitude of four.
examples.cn: 这个三角形的底为六厘米，高为四厘米。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「爱踢土」——爱踢土，站得高才踢得到，量的是海拔

root: 拉丁语 altus（高的）+ -tudo（名词后缀，表性质或度量），经法语 altitude 进入英语，核心是「以某条基准线量出的高度」。

sensesIntro.en: The senses share one vertical measure: above the sea, above the ground, or above the base of a figure.
sensesIntro.cn: 各义项共享同一种垂直度量：高出海面、高出地面，或高出图形底边。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vertical line is dropped from a high point and measured against a base.
core.cn: 核心意象：从高处垂下一条竖线，以某个底为基准来量。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: the first sense is the vertical distance above sea level or ground.
branches.cn: 度量线：第一个义项是高出海平面或地面的垂直距离。

branches.en: THE GROUND: the second sense turns the measure into a region.
branches.cn: 高地线：第二个义项把度量变成一个地区。

branches.en: THE TRIANGLE: the third sense keeps the same line inside geometry.
branches.cn: 三角线：第三个义项把同一条线留在几何里。

branches.en: THE BASE: both senses need a starting line to measure from.
branches.cn: 基线：两个义项都需要一条起算线。

branches.en: THE THIN AIR: height and high land share the same physical effect.
branches.cn: 稀薄线：高度与高地共享同一种物理效果。

intro.en: Altitude is a Latin noun with a small but clear family built on altus.
intro.cn: altitude 是拉丁名词，围绕 altus 有一个小而清晰的词族。

latinIntro.en: The base altus and the noun suffix -tudo are the Latin elements behind the word.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 altus 与名词后缀 -tudo 是这个词背后的拉丁成分。

items.example: The altitude was recorded on the map.
The altimeter showed five thousand feet.
She sings alto in the choir.

items.meaning: the steady height of a flight
items.example: The jet reached its cruising altitude.
items.exampleCN: 喷气机达到了巡航高度。

definition_zh: 完全地；总共；总而言之
definition_en: completely, in total, or considering everything
core_image: 把散落的物件全部拢成一堆，再一起称重
scene: 预算表列到最后一行，会计把各项数字加了起来。The trip cost two thousand dollars altogether.
sceneCN: 这里 altogether 是「总共」（第 2 个义项：把各项加在一起计算总数）；句意为这趟旅行总共花了两千美元。

pos.zh: 副词：完全地；总共；总而言之

derivatives.zh: 同源成分，义为「全部的」，altogether 的第一部分即来自它
同源成分，义为「一起」，altogether 的第二部分即来自它
由 together 加 -ness 构成，义为「亲密无间；团聚」

senses.title: Completely
senses.definition: entirely, used to emphasize that something is wholly the case
senses.definitionCN: 完全地，用于强调某事整个就是那样
senses.example: The idea is altogether too risky for a first attempt.
senses.exampleCN: 对第一次尝试来说，这个想法实在太冒险了。
senses.why: The phrase meant 'all gathered together'; gathering everything into one heap leaves nothing outside, and that is completeness.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语原意为「全部聚到一起」；把一切都拢成一堆，外面就什么都不剩，这就是「完全」。

senses.title: In total
senses.definition: counting every part or person as one sum
senses.definitionCN: 把每一部分或每个人都计入同一个总数
senses.example: There were forty students altogether in the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 大厅里总共有四十名学生。
senses.why: The same heap can be counted: put all the items in one place, then add them up.
senses.whyCN: 同一堆东西也可以拿来数：把所有项目放在一处，再把它们加起来。

senses.title: Considering everything
senses.definition: used to give a general judgement after weighing all the facts
senses.definitionCN: 在权衡全部事实之后给出总体判断
senses.example: Altogether, the journey was a success.
senses.exampleCN: 总的来说，这次旅程是成功的。
senses.why: When all facts are gathered on one table, the speaker can look at the whole pile and judge it as a whole.
senses.whyCN: 当所有事实都被摆到一张桌上，说话人就能看着整堆东西，对它作整体判断。

intro.en: Altogether is a fused English phrase, and each of its senses is a different way of gathering things into one place.
intro.cn: altogether 是融合的英语短语，它的每个义项都是把事物聚到一处的一种方式。

items.en: Eall meant 'all, wholly', and it survives as the modern word all.
items.cn: eall 意为「全部、完全」，至今仍以现代词 all 存在。

items.en: Togadere meant 'together, in one company or place'.
items.cn: togadere 意为「一起，在同一群或同一处」。

items.en: The two words fused into al togadere, later altogether.
items.cn: 两个词融合为 al togadere，后来成为 altogether。

items.en: Altogether is recorded from the fourteenth century with the sense of 'all together'.
items.cn: altogether 自十四世纪有记录，含义是「全部一起」。

items.en: From 'all together in one place' came 'counted as one total'.
items.cn: 从「全部聚在一处」产生了「合起来算作一个总数」。

items.en: The same phrase also meant 'entirely', and both senses survived into modern use.
items.cn: 同一短语也意为「完全」，两个义项都活到了现代。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the two parts and the often-confused phrase; the near-meaning group gathers total and completeness adverbs.
note.cn: 形近组收两个成分与常被混淆的短语；近义组收总数与完全类副词。

entries.definition: The phrase meaning everyone in one group or at one time.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，意为所有人聚在一组或同一时间。

entries.definition: In company or in one place.
entries.definitionCN: 指在一起或在一处。

entries.definition: The whole number or amount.
entries.definitionCN: 指全部的数量。

entries.definition: In every respect, with nothing missing.
entries.definitionCN: 指在每个方面，毫无缺失。

entries.definition: Wholly, often in negative or cautious statements.
entries.definitionCN: 指完全地，常用于否定或谨慎的表述。

entries.definition: When everything is added up.
entries.definitionCN: 指把所有东西加起来时。

entries.definition: Considering all facts, generally.
entries.definitionCN: 指考虑全部事实后，总体而言。

normalIntro.en: These hooks gather everything into one pile and then read the pile three ways.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子把一切拢成一堆，再从三个角度读这一堆。

normal.en: Altogether is all together: everything in one heap.
normal.cn: altogether 就是 all together：所有东西拢成一堆。

normal.en: If nothing is outside the heap, the word means completely.
normal.cn: 如果堆外什么都不剩，这个词就意为「完全」。

normal.en: If you count the heap, it means in total.
normal.cn: 如果你数这一堆，它就意为「总共」。

normal.en: If you judge the heap, it means on the whole.
normal.cn: 如果你评判这一堆，它就意为「总而言之」。

normal.en: Keep all together as two words when you mean a group; use one word when you mean a sum.
normal.cn: 表示一群人时，all together 分写；表示总数时，altogether 连写。

abstract.en: Picture coins scattered across a table and swept into one pile.
abstract.cn: 想象硬币散在桌上，被扫成一堆。

abstract.en: Now picture the pile weighed, counted and judged at once.
abstract.cn: 再想象这堆硬币同时被称重、清点与评判。

abstract.en: That single pile is the whole life of altogether.
abstract.cn: 这一堆，就是 altogether 的全部生命。

examples.en: The weather was altogether unsuitable for sailing.
examples.cn: 这种天气完全不适合航行。

examples.en: There were thirty guests altogether at the dinner.
examples.cn: 晚宴上总共有三十位客人。

examples.en: Altogether, it was a useful meeting.
examples.cn: 总的来说，这是一次有用的会议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，特盖德」——哦，特地盖到一起，全都聚在一处

root: 古英语 eall（全部）+ togædere（一起）融合为 al togadere，再缩为 altogether，核心是「全部聚到一处」，由此生出「完全」「总共」「总体」三义。

sensesIntro.en: One heap yields three readings: nothing outside it, its counted sum, and the judgement of the whole.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一堆东西给出三种读法：堆外无物、数出的总数，以及对整体的判断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: scattered pieces are swept into one pile on a table.
core.cn: 核心意象：散落的碎片被扫成桌上的一堆。

branches.en: THE WHOLE: the first sense says no part escapes the pile.
branches.cn: 整体线：第一个义项说没有任何部分逃出这一堆。

branches.en: THE COUNT: the second sense adds every piece into one figure.
branches.cn: 计数线：第二个义项把每一片都加进同一个数字。

branches.en: THE VIEW: the third sense looks at the pile and judges it.
branches.cn: 视角线：第三个义项看着这一堆并作出判断。

branches.en: THE EMPHASIS: both completeness and general judgement lean on the whole.
branches.cn: 强调线：完全与总体判断都倚重「整体」。

branches.en: THE BALANCE: counting and judging both require every part to be present.
branches.cn: 平衡线：计数与评判都要求每一部分都在场。

intro.en: Altogether is a fused phrase, so the list gathers its parts, its look-alike phrase and its common frames.
intro.cn: altogether 是融合短语，条目收集它的成分、易混短语与常用框架。

latinIntro.en: Both parts are native English, so the Latin entry list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 两个部分都是本土英语，因此拉丁条目为空。

items.example: It was altogether a fine day.
The price is altogether too high.
This is an altogether different problem.
items.exampleCN: 这是一个完全不同的问题。
假期让一家人团聚在一起。

definition_zh: 铝；铝制品；铝制的
definition_en: a light, silvery metal that resists rust and is used in foil, cans, and aircraft
core_image: 一卷银亮的薄箔，轻得几乎不压手
scene: 厨房里翻出一卷银亮的箔纸，准备包住鱼。She wrapped the fish in aluminium foil before baking it.
sceneCN: 这里 aluminium 是「铝」（第 1 个义项：一种轻而银白的金属元素）；句意为她在烤鱼前用铝箔把鱼包起来。

pos.zh: 名词：铝
形容词：铝制的

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁 alumen（明矾）加 -ous 构成，义为「含铝的；明矾的」
由 alumen 演变的化学名词，义为「氧化铝」
由 aluminium 加 -ize 构成，义为「给……镀铝」
由 aluminize 加 -ation 构成，义为「镀铝工艺」

senses.title: The metal element
senses.definition: a chemical element, a light silvery metal with the symbol Al
senses.definitionCN: 一种化学元素，符号为 Al 的轻质银白色金属
senses.example: The bicycle frame is made of aluminium.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆自行车的车架是铝制的。
senses.why: The name was coined from alum, the mineral salt that first made the metal known; a metal named after its ore keeps the ore's story.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字由明矾而来，最初正是这种矿物盐让人认识了该金属；以矿石命名的金属保留着矿石的故事。

senses.title: The metal as a material
senses.definition: used before another noun for objects or materials made of this metal
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词前，指用这种金属制成的物品或材料
senses.example: He crushed the empty aluminium can and put it in the bin.
senses.exampleCN: 他把空铝罐捏扁，丢进垃圾桶。
senses.why: The element becomes a material when it is shaped; foil, cans and frames are the metal seen as something you can hold.
senses.whyCN: 元素一旦被塑形就成为材料；箔、罐与框架，就是被当作可拿在手里的金属。

intro.en: Aluminium is a modern name built on an ancient word for alum, and its spelling split across the Atlantic.
intro.cn: aluminium 是建立在古老「明矾」一词上的现代名称，它的拼写横跨大西洋分成了两派。

items.en: Alumen meant 'alum', the bitter mineral salt used in dyeing and medicine.
items.cn: alumen 意为「明矾」，是染色与医药中使用的苦涩矿物盐。

items.en: Alum was a valuable mordant in the cloth trade, and its name travelled with the trade.
items.cn: 明矾在布匹贸易中是珍贵的媒染剂，它的名字也随贸易流传。

items.en: Alumina, the oxide of the metal, was named from alum before the metal itself was isolated.
items.cn: alumina 即该金属的氧化物，在金属本身被分离之前就已由明矾得名。

items.en: Davy proposed the name aluminium in 1812, and the metal soon became common.
items.cn: 戴维在 1812 年提出 aluminium 这个名称，这种金属很快普及。

items.en: British usage kept Davy's -ium; American usage shortened the word to aluminum.
items.cn: 英式用法保留了戴维的 -ium；美式用法则把词缩短为 aluminum。

items.en: The metal now names foil, cans, aircraft frames and window frames.
items.cn: 这种金属如今命名了箔、罐、飞机框架与窗框。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the mineral and spelling relatives; the near-meaning group gathers metal and material words.
note.cn: 形近组收矿物与拼写亲属；近义组收金属与材料类词。

entries.definition: The American spelling and pronunciation of the same metal.
entries.definitionCN: 同一种金属的美式拼写与读音。

entries.definition: The oxide of aluminium, a white powder.
entries.definitionCN: 铝的氧化物，一种白色粉末。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning containing alum or aluminium.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「含明矾或铝的」。

entries.definition: The general class of shiny, conductive elements.
entries.definitionCN: 指有光泽、可导电的一类元素。

entries.definition: A very thin sheet of metal used for wrapping.
entries.definitionCN: 指用于包裹的极薄金属片。

entries.definition: A metal mixed with another element to improve it.
entries.definitionCN: 指与其他元素混合以改善性能的金属。

entries.definition: The ore from which aluminium is extracted.
entries.definitionCN: 指提炼铝所用的矿石。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a roll of silver foil and then move to ore, element and spelling.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一卷银色箔纸开始，再移到矿石、元素与拼写。

normal.en: Aluminium begins like alum, because alum is where the metal was first found.
normal.cn: aluminium 开头像 alum（明矾），因为这种金属最初就是从明矾中认识的。

normal.en: The -ium ending marks a metal, like sodium and calcium.
normal.cn: -ium 结尾标记一种金属，如 sodium 与 calcium。

normal.en: British aluminium keeps the i; American aluminum drops it.
normal.cn: 英式 aluminium 保留那个 i；美式 aluminum 丢掉它。

normal.en: Foil, cans and frames are the metal in everyday shapes.
normal.cn: 箔、罐与框架，就是这种金属的日常形状。

normal.en: Aluminium is light, so aircraft and bicycles love it.
normal.cn: 铝很轻，所以飞机与自行车都喜欢它。

abstract.en: Picture a white mineral in a dyer's workshop, bitter and rough.
abstract.cn: 想象染坊里一块白色矿石，苦涩而粗糙。

abstract.en: Now picture that mineral heated until a silver drop appears.
abstract.cn: 再想象那块矿石被加热，直到出现一滴银色金属。

abstract.en: Roll the drop thin and it becomes the foil on your kitchen shelf.
abstract.cn: 把那滴金属轧薄，它就变成厨房架子上的箔纸。

examples.en: The window frames are made of aluminium.
examples.cn: 这些窗框是铝制的。

examples.en: Aluminium foil keeps the sandwich fresh.
examples.cn: 铝箔能让三明治保持新鲜。

examples.en: The factory recycles aluminium cans by the ton.
examples.cn: 这家工厂成吨地回收铝罐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿鲁米尼恩」——阿，鲁米尼恩，银亮的铝箔卷

root: 由拉丁语 alumen（明矾）演变而来；铝的氧化物 alumina 先得名，1808 年戴维据其提出 aluminium，英式保留 -ium，美式缩为 aluminum。

sensesIntro.en: The two senses are the element and the element as a workable material.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项分别是元素本身，以及作为可加工材料的该元素。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a silver roll of foil lies on a kitchen shelf, almost weightless.
core.cn: 核心意象：厨房架子上放着一卷银色箔纸，几乎感觉不到重量。

branches.en: THE ELEMENT: the first sense is the metal itself with its symbol Al.
branches.cn: 元素线：第一个义项是带有符号 Al 的金属本身。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL: the second sense treats the metal as something shaped and used.
branches.cn: 材料线：第二个义项把这种金属当作可塑形、可使用的东西。

branches.en: THE ROLL: foil is the element at its thinnest and most familiar.
branches.cn: 箔卷线：箔是这种元素最薄、最熟悉的形态。

branches.en: THE RECYCLING: cans and frames return the material to the metal.
branches.cn: 回收线：罐与框架把材料又送回金属。

branches.en: THE NAME: the ore's name still sits inside the element's name.
branches.cn: 名字线：矿石的名字仍留在这个元素名里。

intro.en: Aluminium is a modern scientific name whose family is built on the alum root and the metal suffix.
intro.cn: aluminium 是现代科学名称，词族建立在明矾词根与金属后缀上。

latinIntro.en: The Latin word alumen is the mineral source behind the name.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 alumen 是这个名称背后的矿物来源。

items.exampleCN: 氧化铝是一种白色粉末。

items.example: Aluminum foil is common in kitchens.
The frame uses a light aluminium alloy.

definition_zh: 总是；始终；永远；老是
definition_en: at all times, forever, or on every occasion, sometimes with annoyance
core_image: 同一条路，每一次都走同一边
scene: 他每天清晨都去河边跑步，风雨无阻。She always walks to school, even in winter.
sceneCN: 这里 always 是「总是；始终」（第 1 个义项：在每一次情形下都如此）；句意为她总是步行上学，冬天也不例外。

pos.zh: 副词：总是；始终；永远；老是

derivatives.zh: 同源成分，义为「全部的」，always 的第一部分即来自它
同源成分，义为「路；方式」，always 的历史第二部分即来自它
由 always 与 on 构成的复合形容词，义为「始终在线的；常开的」

senses.title: On every occasion
senses.definition: every time a particular situation occurs, with no exceptions
senses.definitionCN: 每当特定情形出现时都如此，没有例外
senses.example: The shop always opens at seven in the morning.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店总是在早上七点开门。
senses.why: The old phrase ealne weg meant 'all the way'; if a habit holds for the whole way, it holds on every occasion along it.
senses.whyCN: 古短语 ealne weg 意为「整条路」；若一个习惯贯穿整条路，它在这条路上的每一次都成立。

senses.title: For all time
senses.definition: for ever, through all time, without ending
senses.definitionCN: 永远、贯穿全部时间、没有终点
senses.example: The old tower will always stand above the river.
senses.exampleCN: 那座古塔将永远立在河上方。
senses.why: If the way has no end, the statement has no end either: 'all the way' becomes 'for all time'.
senses.whyCN: 如果这条路没有尽头，这句话也没有尽头：「整条路」就变成「永远」。

senses.title: Repeatedly, often with annoyance
senses.definition: used with a progressive verb to complain about a repeated habit
senses.definitionCN: 与进行时连用，抱怨某种反复出现的习惯
senses.example: He is always losing his keys on the way out.
senses.exampleCN: 他出门时老是把钥匙弄丢。
senses.why: A habit repeated without a break can become a nuisance, so the same word carries a complaint when paired with the progressive.
senses.whyCN: 不断重复的习惯会变成麻烦，因此这个词与进行时搭配时，就带上了抱怨。

intro.en: Always grew out of a phrase about a road, and its senses still follow that road to its end.
intro.cn: always 从一个关于道路的短语生长出来，它的义项仍沿着那条路走到尽头。

items.en: The phrase ealne weg meant 'all the way, the whole journey'.
items.cn: 短语 ealne weg 意为「整条路、整个行程」。

items.en: From 'the whole way' it came to mean 'at every time along the way'.
items.cn: 从「整条路」引申为「在这条路上的每一个时刻」。

items.en: The phrase contracted to alwey, and later the final -s was added.
items.cn: 这个短语缩为 alwey，后来又在词尾加上 -s。

items.en: Always is recorded from the thirteenth century.
items.cn: always 自十三世纪有记录。

items.en: The sense widened to 'for all time, eternally'.
items.cn: 词义扩展到「永远、永恒地」。

items.en: Modern use also marks a repeated habit, sometimes with irritation.
items.cn: 现代用法还标记反复的习惯，有时带有不耐烦。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the source words and the split phrase; the near-meaning group gathers frequency and permanence adverbs.
note.cn: 形近组收来源词与分写短语；近义组收频率与永久类副词。

entries.definition: The phrase meaning every route or method.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，意为每条路线或每种方法。

entries.definition: A road, route, or manner.
entries.definitionCN: 指道路、路线或方式。

entries.definition: The whole of a group or amount.
entries.definitionCN: 指一组或一份量的全部。

entries.definition: For all future time, without end.
entries.definitionCN: 指未来全部时间，没有尽头。

entries.definition: Continuously or very frequently.
entries.definitionCN: 指持续地或非常频繁地。

entries.definition: In every case, without exception.
entries.definitionCN: 指在每种情形下，毫无例外。

entries.definition: Repeatedly, with short breaks.
entries.definitionCN: 指反复地，中间有短暂间隔。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep one road and walk it again, then stretch it into forever and into a complaint.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子保留一条路，一再走它，再把它拉成永远，也拉成抱怨。

normal.en: Always is all plus way: the whole road, every time.
normal.cn: always 是 all 加 way：整条路，每一次。

normal.en: If a habit covers the whole road, it happens on every occasion.
normal.cn: 如果一个习惯覆盖整条路，它就在每个场合都发生。

normal.en: If the road has no end, always means forever.
normal.cn: 如果这条路没有尽头，always 就意为永远。

normal.en: With a progressive verb, always turns into a complaint.
normal.cn: 与进行时连用时，always 就变成抱怨。

normal.en: Keep all ways apart when you mean routes; always is one word for time.
normal.cn: 表示路线时，all ways 分写；表示时间时，always 是一个词。

abstract.en: Picture a single road walked at dawn, at noon and at night.
abstract.cn: 想象同一条路，在清晨、正午与夜里都被走过。

abstract.en: Now picture the road extending past the horizon with no end sign.
abstract.cn: 再想象这条路越过地平线，没有终点牌。

abstract.en: The same road, repeated or endless, is always.
abstract.cn: 同一条路，反复走或走不完，就是 always。

examples.en: He always arrives before eight.
examples.cn: 他总是八点前到。

examples.en: The old clock has always stood in the hall.
examples.cn: 那座旧钟一直立在门厅里。

examples.en: She is always losing her keys.
examples.cn: 她老是把钥匙弄丢。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「欧威兹」——欧，威兹，威风每次都到场

root: 古英语短语 ealne weg（整条路）缩合为 alwey，后加词尾 -s 成为 always；由「整条路」引申出「每次」「永远」，再引申出带不满的「老是」。

sensesIntro.en: The senses follow one road: every time along it, the road without end, and the same step repeated until it irritates.
sensesIntro.cn: 各义项沿着同一条路：路上的每一次、没有尽头的路，以及重复到令人烦的同一个脚步。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same road is walked again and again, always on the same side.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一条路被一再走过，总在同一边。

branches.en: THE ROAD: the first sense covers every occasion along the way.
branches.cn: 道路线：第一个义项覆盖这条路走来的每个场合。

branches.en: THE HORIZON: the second sense removes the end of the road.
branches.cn: 地平线：第二个义项拿掉了路的尽头。

branches.en: THE LOOP: the third sense repeats one step until it annoys.
branches.cn: 循环线：第三个义项把同一个脚步重复到令人烦。

branches.en: THE PATTERN: a habit is simply the road walked often enough to be noticed.
branches.cn: 模式线：习惯不过是被走到足以被注意的那条路。

branches.en: THE STRETCH: both forever and irritation stretch repetition in time.
branches.cn: 延展线：永远与不耐烦都把重复在时间上拉长。

intro.en: Always is a fused phrase, so its list gathers the source words, the split phrase and common frames.
intro.cn: always 是融合短语，条目收集来源词、分写短语与常用框架。

latinIntro.en: The word is native English, so the Latin entry list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属于本土英语，因此拉丁条目为空。

items.example: This way leads to the station.
The menu is always the same.

items.exampleCN: 始终在线的连接费用更高。

definition_zh: 业余爱好者；非专业人士；业余的；外行的
definition_en: a person who takes part in an activity for pleasure rather than for pay, or one who is not a professional
core_image: 下班后换上球衣，只为踢一场开心的球
scene: 周末球场上，一群下班后赶来的球员正在热身。The tournament is open to amateur players of any age.
sceneCN: 这里 amateur 是「业余爱好者」（第 1 个义项：出于兴趣而非为报酬参加活动的人）；句意为这项比赛向任何年龄的业余球员开放。

pos.zh: 名词：业余爱好者；非专业人士
形容词：业余的；外行的

derivatives.zh: 由 amateur 加 -ish 构成，义为「业余水平的；不熟练的」
由 amateurish 加 -ly 构成，义为「以业余水平地」
由 amateur 加 -ism 构成，义为「业余主义；非职业原则」

senses.title: A person who takes part for pleasure
senses.definition: someone who does an activity for enjoyment rather than as a paid profession
senses.definitionCN: 出于兴趣而非作为受薪职业从事某项活动的人
senses.example: He plays the violin as an amateur, not for money.
senses.exampleCN: 他拉小提琴是业余爱好，不为挣钱。
senses.why: French amateur came from Latin amator, 'lover'; the amateur is literally a lover of the activity, and love, not pay, is the motive.
senses.whyCN: 法语 amateur 来自拉丁语 amator「爱者」；业余爱好者字面上就是这项活动的爱者，动机是爱，而不是报酬。

senses.title: Not professional
senses.definition: describing an activity, event, or group that is not paid or organized as a profession
senses.definitionCN: 形容不以报酬或职业方式组织的活动、赛事或团体
senses.example: The amateur league has no paid coaches.
senses.exampleCN: 这个业余联赛没有受薪教练。
senses.why: If the player is a lover rather than a wage earner, the whole league built around such players is called amateur too.
senses.whyCN: 如果参与者是爱者而非挣工资的人，围绕这类人组成的整个联赛也被称为业余的。

senses.title: A person with limited skill
senses.definition: used disapprovingly for someone who does something without proper skill or training
senses.definitionCN: 带贬义，指缺乏适当技能或训练却做某事的人
senses.example: The repairs looked like the work of an amateur.
senses.exampleCN: 这些维修看起来像外行干的。
senses.why: Love without training can leave gaps in skill, so the same word also scolds the person who tries without proper practice.
senses.whyCN: 有爱却无训练，技能就会有缺口，因此同一个词也用来责备未经正规练习就上手的人。

intro.en: Amateur is built on the Latin verb for loving, and the word still asks whether the motive is love or money.
intro.cn: amateur 建立在拉丁语表示「爱」的动词上，这个词至今仍在追问动机是爱还是钱。

items.en: Amare meant 'to love', the source of amateur, amorous and amiable.
items.cn: amare 意为「爱」，是 amateur、amorous 与 amiable 的来源。

items.en: Amator meant 'lover', one who loves a person or an activity.
items.cn: amator 意为「爱者」，指爱一个人或一项活动的人。

items.en: French amateur meant 'lover, enthusiast', and it named someone devoted to an art or sport.
items.cn: 法语 amateur 意为「爱好者、热衷者」，指献身于某门艺术或运动的人。

items.en: English amateur entered in the eighteenth century and soon contrasted with professional.
items.cn: 英语 amateur 于十八世纪进入，很快就与 professional 形成对照。

items.en: Modern sport sharpened the contrast: amateurs played for love, professionals for pay.
items.cn: 现代体育强化了这种对照：业余者为热爱而赛，职业者为报酬而赛。

items.en: The word also took a critical sense for work done without proper training.
items.cn: 这个词还发展出批评义，指未受适当训练而做的工作。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same love root; the near-meaning group gathers non-professionals and enthusiasts.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「爱」词根的词；近义组收非职业者与热衷者。

entries.definition: Done in an unskilled, non-professional way.
entries.definitionCN: 指以不熟练、非专业的方式完成的。

entries.definition: The principle that sport or art should not be paid.
entries.definitionCN: 指体育或艺术不应受薪的原则。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning relating to love or lovers.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「与爱情或恋人有关的」。

entries.definition: A neutral term for someone not paid for the activity.
entries.definitionCN: 中性说法，指未因该活动获得报酬的人。

entries.definition: A person who pursues an activity as a hobby.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某项活动当作爱好的人。

entries.definition: Someone with strong interest in a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 指对某主题有强烈兴趣的人。

entries.definition: A person without professional knowledge in a field.
entries.definitionCN: 指在某一领域没有专业知识的人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with love as the motive and then move to the league and to the critic's judgement.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子以「爱为动机」开始，再移到联赛，最后移到批评者的判断。

normal.en: Amateur hides amator, a lover: the person plays because they love it.
normal.cn: amateur 里藏着 amator，即爱者：这个人因为热爱才参与。

normal.en: Love without pay makes an amateur; pay without love makes a professional.
normal.cn: 有爱而无报酬是业余者；有报酬而无爱是职业者。

normal.en: An amateur league is a league of lovers.
normal.cn: 业余联赛就是一帮爱者的联赛。

normal.en: Amateurish adds a frown: love without enough practice.
normal.cn: amateurish 加上皱眉：有爱却练习不足。

normal.en: If a critic calls you an amateur, the word has stopped meaning lover.
normal.cn: 如果批评者叫你 amateur，这个词就不再是「爱者」的意思了。

abstract.en: Picture a violinist playing after dinner for friends, with no ticket sold.
abstract.cn: 想象一位小提琴手晚饭后为朋友演奏，一张票也没卖。

abstract.en: Now picture a stadium where every player has another job in the morning.
abstract.cn: 再想象一座体育场，每个球员早上都还有另一份工作。

abstract.en: Love is the thread that ties all these pictures to amateur.
abstract.cn: 把所有这些画面系到 amateur 上的线，就是爱。

examples.en: She is an amateur photographer who shoots at weekends.
examples.cn: 她是个周末拍照的业余摄影师。

examples.en: The amateur team beat the professionals in the final.
examples.cn: 业余队在决赛中击败了职业队。

examples.en: His cooking is amateurish but full of heart.
examples.cn: 他做饭水平业余，却很有心。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿玛特」——阿，玛特，爱这个才玩，不为钱

root: 拉丁语 amare（爱）→ amator（爱者）→ 法语 amateur（爱好者），十八世纪进入英语；核心是「因爱而做」，与「为报酬而做」的职业者相对。

sensesIntro.en: The senses follow one motive: love of the activity, which can define a person, a whole league, or become a criticism when skill is missing.
sensesIntro.cn: 各义项沿着同一个动机：对活动的爱；它可以定义一个人、一整个联赛，也可以在技能不足时变成批评。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a player puts on a jersey after work and plays for the joy of it.
core.cn: 核心意象：球员下班后换上球衣，只为那份快乐而踢。

branches.en: THE LOVER: the first sense is the person drawn by love of the activity.
branches.cn: 爱者线：第一个义项是被对活动的爱吸引来的人。

branches.en: THE LEAGUE: the second sense extends the person to the whole unpaid system.
branches.cn: 联赛线：第二个义项把人扩展到整个无报酬体系。

branches.en: THE CRITIC: the third sense turns missing training into a label.
branches.cn: 批评线：第三个义项把缺失的训练变成一个标签。

branches.en: THE GAP: love and skill can separate, and the word marks both ends.
branches.cn: 缺口线：爱与技能可能分开，这个词标记两端。

branches.en: THE STANDARD: professional pay and trained skill are the two measures behind the word.
branches.cn: 标准线：职业报酬与受训技能是这个词背后的两把尺。

intro.en: Amateur is a French borrowing from the Latin love root, with a family of suffixes around it.
intro.cn: amateur 是源自拉丁「爱」词根的法语借词，周围有一族后缀派生词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base amare and the noun amator stand behind the word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 amare 与名词 amator 站在这个词背后。

items.exampleCN: 旧规则强制执行业余原则。

items.example: He plays in an amateur league.
items.exampleCN: 他在一个业余联赛踢球。

items.meaning: the state of not being paid

definition_zh: 使惊奇；使大为赞叹；使困惑
definition_en: to fill someone with great surprise or wonder
core_image: 眼前的一幕超出预料，人一下子愣在原地
scene: 观众看到魔术师从空帽子里抽出一束花。The trick never failed to amaze the children.
sceneCN: 这里 amaze 是「使惊奇」（第 1 个义项：让人产生强烈的惊讶与赞叹）；句意为这个戏法总能让孩子们惊叹。

pos.zh: 及物动词：使惊奇；使大为赞叹

derivatives.zh: 由 amaze 加 -ed 构成，义为「感到惊奇的」
由 amaze 加 -ing 构成，义为「令人惊叹的」
由 amazing 加 -ly 构成，义为「令人惊叹地；极其」
由 amaze 加 -ment 构成，义为「惊奇；惊愕」

senses.title: To fill with wonder
senses.definition: to surprise someone very much, often in a pleasant or impressive way
senses.definitionCN: 使某人非常惊讶，常带愉快或令人印象深刻的意味
senses.example: The view from the summit amazed every climber.
senses.exampleCN: 山顶的景色让每个登山者都惊叹。
senses.why: Old English amasian meant 'to confound, bewilder'; wonder and confusion began as the same stunned state.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 amasian 意为「使慌乱、使迷惑」；惊叹与困惑最初是同一种被震住的状态。

senses.title: To astonish beyond belief
senses.titleCN: 使大为震惊；使难以置信
senses.definition: to astonish someone so much that the fact seems hard to believe
senses.definitionCN: 使某人极为震惊，以至于事实显得难以相信
senses.example: It amazes me that she finished the race with a broken shoe.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿着坏掉的鞋跑完全程，这让我大为震惊。
senses.why: The same stunned state can tip from wonder into disbelief when the fact itself seems impossible.
senses.whyCN: 当事实本身显得不可能时，同一种被震住的状态就会从惊叹滑向难以置信。

intro.en: Amaze began as a word for being stunned and confused, and its family still keeps a maze inside.
intro.cn: amaze 最初指被震住、被弄糊涂，它的词族里至今藏着一座迷宫。

items.en: Amasian meant 'to confound, bewilder', to leave someone unable to think clearly.
items.cn: amasian 意为「使慌乱、使迷惑」，让人无法清楚思考。

items.en: The initial a- is an old intensive or prepositional prefix, not the article a.
items.cn: 开头的 a- 是古老的加强或介词性前缀，并非冠词 a。

items.en: Middle English amasen softened the old confusion toward surprise and wonder.
items.cn: 中古英语 amasen 把古老的「慌乱」软化为惊讶与惊叹。

items.en: By the sixteenth century amaze clearly meant to astonish, and the verb became common.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，amaze 明确表示「使震惊」，这个动词变得常用。

items.en: The old word is related to maze, a place where a person loses the way, the same image of being lost.
items.cn: 这个古词与 maze 有关，后者指让人迷路的地方，共享同一种「迷失」意象。

items.en: Modern English keeps amazed for the person and amazing for the thing that causes it.
items.cn: 现代英语用 amazed 指人，用 amazing 指引起惊讶的事物。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the maze root and the derived forms; the near-meaning group gathers stronger and weaker surprise verbs.
note.cn: 形近组收 maze 词根与派生形式；近义组收强弱不同的「使惊讶」动词。

entries.definition: A network of paths where a person can lose the way.
entries.definitionCN: 指让人迷路的复杂路径网络。

entries.definition: Causing great surprise or wonder.
entries.definitionCN: 指引起强烈惊讶或惊叹的。

entries.definition: The state of being greatly surprised.
entries.definitionCN: 指极度惊讶的状态。

entries.definition: To surprise very greatly, often with a shock.
entries.definitionCN: 指使人极为惊讶，常带震动感。

entries.definition: To shock with surprise, stronger than amaze.
entries.definitionCN: 指以惊讶震动人心，语气比 amaze 更强。

entries.definition: To cause admiration, with less of the stunned element.
entries.definitionCN: 指引起钦佩，被震住的程度较弱。

entries.definition: To leave someone unable to react.
entries.definitionCN: 指使人一时无法反应。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin inside a maze, where confusion and wonder are the same stunned face.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从迷宫内部开始，在那里困惑与惊叹是同一张被震住的脸。

normal.en: Amaze shares a root with maze: both leave a person lost.
normal.cn: amaze 与 maze 共享词根：两者都让人迷失。

normal.en: A maze stops the feet; amaze stops the mind.
normal.cn: 迷宫让脚停下来；amaze 让脑子停下来。

normal.en: Amazed describes the person; amazing describes the thing.
normal.cn: amazed 描述人；amazing 描述事物。

normal.en: Wonder is confusion that turned pleasant.
normal.cn: 惊叹就是变得愉快的困惑。

normal.en: If the fact seems impossible, amaze becomes disbelief.
normal.cn: 如果事实显得不可能，amaze 就变成难以置信。

abstract.en: Picture a walker who turns a corner and finds the path doubled.
abstract.cn: 想象一个行人转过弯，发现路变成了两条。

abstract.en: Now picture the same walker smiling at the trick instead of fearing it.
abstract.cn: 再想象同一个行人对着这个把戏微笑，而不是害怕。

abstract.en: That smile is the moment confusion becomes amaze.
abstract.cn: 那个微笑，就是困惑变成 amaze 的瞬间。

examples.en: The fireworks amazed the crowd.
examples.cn: 烟花让全场惊叹。

examples.en: I was amazed at how quickly she learned the language.
examples.cn: 她学这门语言之快让我惊叹。

examples.en: It amazes me that the old bridge still carries trucks.
examples.cn: 那座老桥还能承载卡车，这让我大为惊讶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啊妹子」——啊，妹子一出现，全场都惊呆了

root: 古英语 amasian（使慌乱、使迷惑），带古老加强前缀 a-；与 maze（迷宫）同源，核心是「让人迷失、被震住」，后专指「使惊叹」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses share one stunned state; the first leans toward wonder, the second toward disbelief.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项共享同一种被震住的状态；第一个偏向惊叹，第二个偏向难以置信。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scene exceeds expectation, and the viewer freezes on the spot.
core.cn: 核心意象：眼前一幕超出预料，观看者当场愣住。

branches.en: THE WONDER: the first sense is surprise that pleases and impresses.
branches.cn: 惊叹线：第一个义项是令人愉快、令人印象深刻的惊讶。

branches.en: THE IMPOSSIBLE: the second sense is surprise that refuses belief.
branches.cn: 不可能线：第二个义项是拒绝相信的惊讶。

branches.en: THE FREEZE: both senses stop the mind for a moment.
branches.cn: 定格线：两个义项都让头脑停顿片刻。

branches.en: THE MAZE: the old confusion survives as wonder.
branches.cn: 迷宫线：古老的困惑以惊叹的形式存活下来。

branches.en: THE SHOCK: disbelief is the sharper edge of the same state.
branches.cn: 震动线：难以置信是同一种状态更锋利的边缘。

intro.en: Amaze is an old English verb, and its modern family is built with common participial and noun suffixes.
intro.cn: amaze 是古老的英语动词，现代词族由常见的分词与名词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The word is native English, so no Latin entry is listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属于本土英语，因此不列拉丁条目。

items.example: She was amazed by the size.
items.exampleCN: 她对这个尺寸感到惊奇。
这是一场令人惊叹的表演。

items.example: The view never fails to amaze.
We were amazed at the speed.
items.exampleCN: 我们对这个速度感到惊奇。

definition_zh: 女大使；女大使夫人
definition_en: a woman who is an ambassador, or historically the wife of an ambassador
core_image: 使馆门口，一位女士代表国家迎接宾客
scene: 使馆晚宴前，一位女外交官站在门口迎接客人。The ambassadress greeted the guests at the embassy door.
sceneCN: 这里 ambassadress 是「女大使」（第 1 个义项：担任大使职务的女性）；句意为这位女大使在使馆门口迎接客人。

pos.zh: 名词：女大使；女大使夫人

derivatives.zh: 基础名词，义为「大使」，ambassadress 由它加阴性后缀构成
由 ambassador 加 -ial 构成，义为「大使的；大使级的」
同源名词，义为「大使馆；大使馆全体人员」

senses.title: A woman serving as ambassador
senses.definition: a woman who holds the official rank of ambassador and represents her country abroad
senses.definitionCN: 担任大使正式职衔、在国外代表本国的女性
senses.example: The ambassadress presented her credentials at the palace.
senses.exampleCN: 这位女大使在宫殿递交了国书。
senses.why: The -ess suffix once marked a woman holding the same office; ambassadress is simply ambassador with that old feminine ending.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ess 曾标记担任同一职务的女性；ambassadress 就是 ambassador 加上这个古老的阴性词尾。

senses.title: The wife of an ambassador
senses.definition: a historical use for the wife of an ambassador, especially when she had a formal social role
senses.definitionCN: 历史上指大使的妻子，尤其当她承担正式社交职责时
senses.example: In the old photographs, the ambassadress stands beside the ambassador.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧照片里，大使夫人站在大使身旁。
senses.why: When diplomatic life assigned a public role to the ambassador's wife, the feminine form named that role rather than the office.
senses.whyCN: 当外交生活给大使的妻子分配了公开角色时，这个阴性形式命名的就是那个角色，而不是官职。

intro.en: Ambassadress is ambassador plus an old feminine ending, and the word carries the history of diplomatic titles.
intro.cn: ambassadress 是 ambassador 加上古老的阴性词尾，这个词带着外交头衔的历史。

items.en: Ambactus meant 'servant, retainer', a word borrowed into Latin from a Celtic source.
items.cn: ambactus 意为「仆人、随从」，是拉丁语从凯尔特语借入的词。

items.en: Old French ambassadeur named an envoy sent on a mission.
items.cn: 古法语 ambassadeur 指被派去执行使命的使节。

items.en: English ambassador entered in the fourteenth century as the title of a senior envoy.
items.cn: 英语 ambassador 于十四世纪进入，指高级使节的头衔。

items.en: The French feminine suffix -esse was added to make ambassadress, first for the wife and later for a woman in the office.
items.cn: 加上法语阴性后缀 -esse 构成 ambassadress，最初指大使夫人，后来也指担任该职务的女性。

items.en: The form is recorded in English from the eighteenth century and was common in formal writing.
items.cn: 这个形式自十八世纪在英语中有记录，并在正式书面语中常见。

items.en: Today many writers prefer ambassador for both sexes, and ambassadress sounds old or ceremonial.
items.cn: 今天许多作者对两性都用 ambassador，ambassadress 听起来古老或带仪式感。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the diplomatic family; the near-meaning group gathers envoys and diplomats.
note.cn: 形近组收外交词族；近义组收使节与外交官。

entries.definition: The base title for a senior envoy.
entries.definitionCN: 指高级使节的基础头衔。

entries.definition: The office or residence of an ambassador.
entries.definitionCN: 指大使的办公处或官邸。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning relating to an ambassador.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「大使的」。

entries.definition: A messenger or representative sent on a mission.
entries.definitionCN: 指被派执行使命的使者或代表。

entries.definition: An official who represents a country abroad.
entries.definitionCN: 指在国外代表本国的官员。

entries.definition: A senior diplomat, often below an ambassador in rank.
entries.definitionCN: 指高级外交官，级别通常低于大使。

entries.definition: A person chosen to speak or act for a group.
entries.definitionCN: 指被选出来为团体发言或行事的人。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with the ambassador title and then add the old feminine ending.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从 ambassador 头衔开始，再加上古老的阴性词尾。

normal.en: Ambassadress is ambassador plus -ess, the old mark of a woman.
normal.cn: ambassadress 就是 ambassador 加上 -ess，这个古老的女性标记。

normal.en: The word first named the ambassador's wife, then a woman holding the office.
normal.cn: 这个词先指大使夫人，后指担任该职务的女性。

normal.en: Embassy is the building; ambassador is the title; ambassadress is the old feminine title.
normal.cn: embassy 是建筑；ambassador 是头衔；ambassadress 是古老的阴性头衔。

normal.en: Modern style often drops the -ess and calls everyone ambassador.
normal.cn: 现代文体常去掉 -ess，对所有人都用 ambassador。

normal.en: Picture the embassy door, with a woman receiving guests in the name of her country.
normal.cn: 想象使馆门口，一位女士以国家的名义迎接宾客。

abstract.en: Picture a formal hall where a title is handed over with sealed papers.
abstract.cn: 想象一座正式大厅，头衔随密封文书一同交接。

abstract.en: Now picture the same hall a century later, the title shared by both sexes.
abstract.cn: 再想象一个世纪后的同一座大厅，头衔由两性共享。

abstract.en: The old -ess is the fossil the word carries from the first hall.
abstract.cn: 古老的 -ess 就是这个词从第一座大厅带来的化石。

examples.en: The ambassadress opened the cultural exhibition.
examples.cn: 这位女大使为文化展开幕。

examples.en: The ambassadress and her husband hosted the reception.
examples.cn: 女大使和她的丈夫主持了招待会。

examples.en: In the old portrait, the ambassadress wears a formal gown.
examples.cn: 在旧画像里，大使夫人穿着正式长裙。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺拔丝得瑞斯」——俺拔丝，得瑞斯女士，使馆门口迎客

root: 拉丁语 ambactus（仆人、随从）经古法语 ambassadeur 进入英语作 ambassador；再加法语阴性后缀 -esse 构成 ambassadress，先指大使夫人，后指女大使。

sensesIntro.en: The two senses split between the office and the social role: a woman ambassador, or historically the ambassador's wife.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项分在官职与社交角色之间：担任大使的女性，或历史上的大使夫人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a woman stands at the embassy door, receiving guests in the name of her country.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位女士站在使馆门口，以国家的名义迎接宾客。

branches.en: THE OFFICE: the first sense is a woman who holds the rank itself.
branches.cn: 官职线：第一个义项是担任该职衔本身的女性。

branches.en: THE HOUSEHOLD: the second sense is the ambassador's wife in her public role.
branches.cn: 家庭线：第二个义项是大使的妻子在公开角色中。

branches.en: THE DOOR: both senses meet at the embassy entrance.
branches.cn: 门口线：两个义项都在使馆门口相遇。

branches.en: THE OLD TITLE: the wife sense is the older, ceremonial layer.
branches.cn: 旧头衔线：夫人义是更古老、更仪式化的一层。

branches.en: THE NEW TITLE: the office sense is the modern reading.
branches.cn: 新头衔线：官职义是现代读法。

intro.en: Ambassadress is ambassador with a feminine suffix, and its family is the diplomatic vocabulary around it.
intro.cn: ambassadress 是带阴性后缀的 ambassador，词族是它周围的外交词汇。

latinIntro.en: The Latin ambactus is the distant source of the ambassador family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ambactus 是 ambassador 词族的远源。

items.example: The embassy is near the river.
An envoy was sent to negotiate.

items.meaning: the woman ambassador posted to a country
items.example: She became the ambassadress to France.

items.meaning: a woman who once held the post
items.exampleCN: 这位前女大使现在教书。

definition_zh: 模棱两可的；含糊不清的；有多种解释的
definition_en: having more than one possible meaning, or not clear enough to be certain
core_image: 一句话站在两条路口，两条都说得通
scene: 合同里有一句话，双方读出了两种意思。The wording of the clause was ambiguous, so both sides claimed a victory.
sceneCN: 这里 ambiguous 是「模棱两可的」（第 1 个义项：可以有两种或多种解释）；句意为这一条款的措辞模棱两可，所以双方都宣称自己赢了。

pos.zh: 形容词：模棱两可的；含糊不清的；有多种解释的

derivatives.zh: 由 ambiguous 加 -ity 构成，义为「歧义；模棱两可」
由 ambiguous 加 -ly 构成，义为「含糊地；模棱两可地」
由 ambiguous 加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「毫不含糊的」
ambiguity 的复数形式，义为「多处歧义」

senses.title: Open to more than one meaning
senses.definition: able to be understood in two or more different ways
senses.definitionCN: 能够被理解成两种或多种不同意思
senses.example: The sentence is ambiguous because it can mean two opposite things.
senses.exampleCN: 这句话有歧义，因为它可以表示两个相反的意思。
senses.why: Latin ambigere meant 'to wander about, dispute', with ambi- 'both' and agere 'drive'; a word that drives both ways is ambiguous.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ambigere 意为「四处游走、争论」，由 ambi-「两边」与 agere「驱动」构成；朝两边驱动的词就是模棱两可的。

senses.title: Not clear or certain
senses.definition: unclear in intention or meaning, so that no firm conclusion can be drawn
senses.definitionCN: 意图或含义不清楚，因而无法得出确定结论
senses.example: His answer was ambiguous, and nobody knew what he wanted.
senses.exampleCN: 他的回答含糊不清，谁也不知道他想要什么。
senses.why: The same wandering can be a lack of clarity rather than a double meaning: the hearer cannot fix the word to one point.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「游走」也可以不是双关，而是缺乏清晰：听者无法把这个词固定在某一点上。

senses.title: Of doubtful or mixed status
senses.titleCN: 身份不明的；性质难定的
senses.definition: having a position or nature that is not clearly one thing or another
senses.definitionCN: 所处位置或性质不能明确归为这一类或那一类
senses.example: The project has an ambiguous legal status.
senses.exampleCN: 这个项目的法律身份不明确。
senses.why: If a thing stands between two categories, it belongs fully to neither, and that in-between state is also called ambiguous.
senses.whyCN: 如果一物站在两个类别之间，它就不完全属于任何一方，这种中间状态也被称为 ambiguous。

intro.en: Ambiguous comes from a Latin verb for wandering both ways, and its senses keep that image of a word on two roads.
intro.cn: ambiguous 来自拉丁语中表示「朝两边游走」的动词，它的义项保留着「一个词站在两条路上」的意象。

items.en: Ambi- meant 'both, around', the prefix behind ambiguous, ambivalent and ambition.
items.cn: ambi- 意为「两边、周围」，是 ambiguous、ambivalent 与 ambition 背后的前缀。

items.en: Agere meant 'to drive, do, act', the second element of the compound.
items.cn: agere 意为「驱动、做、行动」，是这个复合词的第二成分。

items.en: Ambigere meant 'to go about, wander, dispute', to drive in two directions at once.
items.cn: ambigere 意为「四处走动、游移、争论」，即同时朝两个方向驱动。

items.en: The adjective ambiguus described something that could be taken either way.
items.cn: 形容词 ambiguus 描述可以被理解为任一方向的事物。

items.en: French ambigu carried the adjective into English.
items.cn: 法语 ambigu 把这个形容词带入英语。

items.en: English ambiguous settled in the sixteenth century and later extended to unclear status.
items.cn: 英语 ambiguous 在十六世纪固定下来，后来又扩展到「身份不明」的用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same-root family; the near-meaning group gathers unclear and double-edged words.
note.cn: 形近组收同根词族；近义组收含糊与双面类词。

entries.definition: The state of having more than one meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 指具有多种含义的状态。

entries.definition: In a way that can be understood more than one way.
entries.definitionCN: 指以可被多种方式理解的方式。

entries.definition: Having mixed feelings about something.
entries.definitionCN: 指对某事怀有矛盾情感。

entries.definition: Not easy to understand, without the sense of double meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 指不易理解，不带双关意味。

entries.definition: Not precise or definite.
entries.definitionCN: 指不精确、不确定。

entries.definition: Deliberately open to two interpretations.
entries.definitionCN: 指有意保留两种解释。

entries.definition: Not known or not decided.
entries.definitionCN: 指未知或未决定的。

normalIntro.en: These hooks keep a word standing at a fork and then turn the fork into unclear status.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子让一个词站在岔口，再把岔口变成不明身份。

normal.en: Ambi means both: ambiguous drives the meaning both ways.
normal.cn: ambi 意为两边：ambiguous 把意思朝两边驱动。

normal.en: A sentence at a fork can be walked down either road.
normal.cn: 站在岔口的句子，两条路都走得通。

normal.en: Ambiguity is the noun for that fork.
normal.cn: ambiguity 就是那个岔口的名词。

normal.en: Unambiguous means the fork has been closed.
normal.cn: unambiguous 意为岔口已被封上。

normal.en: An ambiguous status is a thing standing between two categories.
normal.cn: ambiguous status 就是站在两个类别之间的东西。

abstract.en: Picture a signpost with two arrows pointing opposite ways, both marked true.
abstract.cn: 想象一块路牌，两个箭头指向相反方向，却都标着「真」。

abstract.en: Now picture a traveller unable to choose, standing still at the post.
abstract.cn: 再想象一个旅人无法选择，站在路牌旁不动。

abstract.en: The stillness of that traveller is what ambiguous describes.
abstract.cn: 那个旅人的静止，就是 ambiguous 所描述的状态。

examples.en: The instructions were ambiguous, so we asked for clarification.
examples.cn: 说明含糊不清，所以我们请求澄清。

examples.en: She gave an ambiguous smile that could mean yes or no.
examples.cn: 她露出一个模棱两可的微笑，可以表示同意，也可以表示不同意。

examples.en: The island has an ambiguous place in the region's history.
examples.cn: 这座岛在该地区的历史中身份不明。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺必归格斯」——俺必归，格斯却说不清归哪边

root: 拉丁语 ambi-（两边）+ agere（驱动）→ ambigere（四处游走、争论）→ ambiguus（可两解的），经法语 ambigu 进入英语；核心是「一个词朝两边走」。

sensesIntro.en: The senses share one fork: double meaning, missing clarity, and a thing that belongs to neither side.
sensesIntro.cn: 各义项共享同一个岔口：双关含义、缺少清晰，以及不属于任何一边的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single word stands at a fork, and both roads can carry its meaning.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个词站在岔口，两条路都能承载它的意思。

branches.en: THE FORK: the first sense is a word that fits two readings.
branches.cn: 岔口线：第一个义项是一个词能装下两种读法。

branches.en: THE FOG: the second sense is a word that fits no firm reading.
branches.cn: 迷雾线：第二个义项是一个词无法固定在任何读法上。

branches.en: THE BORDER: the third sense is a thing that sits between two classes.
branches.cn: 边界线：第三个义项是坐在两个类别之间的事物。

branches.en: THE DOUBLE EDGE: both meaning and clarity are split by the same prefix.
branches.cn: 双刃线：含义与清晰都被同一个前缀劈成两半。

branches.en: THE UNFIXED: unclear speech and unclear status share the same stillness.
branches.cn: 未定线：含糊的言辞与不明的身份共享同一种静止。

intro.en: Ambiguous is a Latin adjective with a productive family of noun, adverb and negative forms.
intro.cn: ambiguous 是拉丁形容词，拥有能产的名词、副词与否定形式词族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin ambi- and agere are the two elements behind ambigere and ambiguus.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ambi- 与 agere 是 ambigere 与 ambiguus 背后的两个成分。

items.exampleCN: ambi- 出现在 ambidextrous 中。
模棱两可的措辞造成了延误。
这个答复是故意含糊的。

definition_zh: 抱负；雄心；志向；追求的目标
definition_en: a strong desire to achieve something, or the goal that such a desire aims at
core_image: 墙上贴着一张远期图纸，人每天朝它多走一步
scene: 年轻工程师把计划书贴在墙上，每天看着它。Her ambition is to build a bridge that can survive any flood.
sceneCN: 这里 ambition 是「抱负；志向」（第 1 个义项：强烈的成就愿望）；句意为她的志向是造一座能经受任何洪水的桥。

pos.zh: 名词：抱负；雄心；志向；追求的目标

derivatives.zh: 由 ambition 加 -ious 构成，义为「有雄心的；野心大的」
由 ambitious 加 -ly 构成，义为「雄心勃勃地」
由 ambitious 加 -ness 构成，义为「雄心；进取心」

senses.title: A strong desire to achieve
senses.definition: the strong drive to succeed, gain power, or reach a high goal
senses.definitionCN: 追求成功、获得权力或达到高目标的强烈动力
senses.example: Her ambition pushed her to study late into the night.
senses.exampleCN: 她的抱负促使她学习到深夜。
senses.why: Latin ambitio first meant canvassing for office, going around the voters; the drive to win office became the general drive to win anything.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ambitio 最初指为竞选公职而四处走访选民；争取官职的动力，变成了争取任何目标的普遍动力。

senses.title: The goal that one aims at
senses.definition: a particular aim or objective that a person strongly wants to reach
senses.definitionCN: 一个人强烈希望达到的特定目标或目的
senses.example: His ambition is to run a small hospital in the mountains.
senses.exampleCN: 他的志向是在山里办一家小医院。
senses.why: The going-around has a destination: the office sought becomes a concrete aim, and that aim is also called an ambition.
senses.whyCN: 这种「四处奔走」有一个目的地：所争取的职位变成一个具体目标，这个目标也被称为 ambition。

senses.title: A desire for power or status
senses.definition: a strong wish for personal advancement, sometimes viewed with disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 对个人晋升的强烈愿望，有时带不赞成的意味
senses.example: His ambition for the top job made him distrust his colleagues.
senses.exampleCN: 他对最高职位的野心让他不信任同事。
senses.why: Canvassing for votes has a shadow side: wanting the office for oneself, and the word can carry that suspicion.
senses.whyCN: 争取选票有阴暗的一面：为自己谋取职位，因此这个词也能带上那种猜疑。

intro.en: Ambition began as a word for walking around to gather votes, and its drive still points at a goal.
intro.cn: ambition 最初指为拉票而四处走动，它的动力至今仍指向一个目标。

items.en: Ambire meant 'to go around', built from ambi- 'around' and ire 'to go'.
items.cn: ambire 意为「四处走」，由 ambi-「周围」与 ire「走」构成。

items.en: Ambitio named the canvassing that candidates did, going around to seek votes.
items.cn: ambitio 指候选人四处走访拉票的行为。

items.en: The adjective ambituosus described a person who sought office eagerly.
items.cn: 形容词 ambituosus 描述急于谋取职位的人。

items.en: French ambition passed the noun into English with the sense of a strong desire for advancement.
items.cn: 法语 ambition 把这个名词带入英语，含义是强烈的上进愿望。

items.en: English ambition first named political striving, then any strong aim.
items.cn: 英语 ambition 先指政治上的争取，后指任何强烈的目标。

items.en: Modern use ranges from admired ambition to the disapproving ambition for power.
items.cn: 现代用法从令人敬佩的抱负，到带贬义的权势野心。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the same-root family; the near-meaning group gathers aims and drives.
note.cn: 形近组收同根词族；近义组收目标与动力类词。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning eager to succeed.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「渴望成功的」。

entries.definition: In an eager, goal-driven way.
entries.definitionCN: 指以急切、目标明确的方式。

entries.definition: The scope or range of something.
entries.definitionCN: 指某事物的范围或界限。

entries.definition: A hope or ambition to achieve something.
entries.definitionCN: 指希望或立志实现某事。

entries.definition: The end result that one aims at.
entries.definitionCN: 指所瞄准的最终结果。

entries.definition: Inner energy that pushes a person forward.
entries.definitionCN: 指推动人向前的内在能量。

entries.definition: A purpose or intention.
entries.definitionCN: 指目的或意图。

normalIntro.en: These hooks walk around the voters, then turn the walk into a goal on the wall.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子先绕选民走一圈，再把这段路变成墙上的目标。

normal.en: Ambition comes from ambire, to go around: first around voters, now around a goal.
normal.cn: ambition 来自 ambire，意为四处走：先绕选民走，现在绕目标走。

normal.en: A candidate walks for votes; a student walks for a degree.
normal.cn: 候选人为了选票奔走；学生为了学位奔走。

normal.en: The destination of that walk is the ambition on the wall.
normal.cn: 这段奔走的目的地，就是墙上的 ambition。

normal.en: Ambition can be praised as drive or blamed as a hunger for power.
normal.cn: ambition 可以被赞为动力，也可以被责为权势欲。

normal.en: Ambitious adds -ious: full of that drive.
normal.cn: ambitious 加上 -ious：充满那股动力。

abstract.en: Picture a candidate crossing a square, shaking every hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一位候选人穿过广场，与每个人握手。

abstract.en: Now picture a teenager crossing the same square toward a distant school.
abstract.cn: 再想象一个少年穿过同一座广场，走向远处的学校。

abstract.en: Both walks are ambition: motion aimed at a destination.
abstract.cn: 两段行走都是 ambition：指向目的地的运动。

examples.en: She has the ambition to become a surgeon.
examples.cn: 她有成为外科医生的抱负。

examples.en: The plan is ambitious but not impossible.
examples.cn: 这个计划雄心勃勃，但并非不可能。

examples.en: His political ambition cost him many friends.
examples.cn: 他的政治野心让他失去了许多朋友。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺必胜」——俺必胜，抱着这股劲往前冲

root: 拉丁语 ambire（四处走，ambi- 周围 + ire 走）→ ambitio（拉票奔走）→ 法语 ambition；由「为谋职位而奔走」引申为「抱负、志向、野心」。

sensesIntro.en: The senses follow one walk: the drive to succeed, the destination it seeks, and the suspicion that the walk is only for oneself.
sensesIntro.cn: 各义项沿着同一段奔走：追求成功的动力、它寻找的目的地，以及「这段奔走只为自己」的猜疑。
